_about: The shared glossary for the findings whitepapers and pages. Each entry: what we mean by the term, the field it comes from, and what it excludes. Papers add their field terms in papers/<id>/terms.json in the same shape; a key used in a paper must exist in one of the two. Edited by hand; the site and the PDFs read the same entries.

preregistration.definition: a dated written plan for a study, fixed and hash-locked before any result is seen: the question, the data, the statistic, the controls, the forecasts and the kill conditions
preregistration.excludes: a plan revised after looking at the outcome, and a protocol written only for the record after the run

planted-check.field: research method; called a positive control in experimental science
planted-check.definition: data built so that the right answer is known, run through the same analysis before the real data, to show that the analysis can see the effect when it is there
planted-check.excludes: any check made on the real data, which cannot show what the analysis misses

control.definition: a version of the data with the structure under test removed (for example shuffled or pooled), scored the same way as the real data, so the real score has something to beat
control.excludes: a comparison with a different dataset or with a published number

null-distribution.definition: the spread of scores a control gives over many random draws; its 95th percentile is the bar a real score must clear
null-distribution.excludes: a theoretical distribution assumed rather than drawn from the data

kill-condition.field: research method (our usage, after Popper's falsification)
kill-condition.definition: a rule written in the preregistration that, when met, decides against the claim with no room for judgement after the run
kill-condition.excludes: reasons found after the run for setting a result aside

void.definition: the verdict of a run whose planted check failed or whose sample fell below its stated minimum; it says nothing for or against the claim
void.excludes: a null result, which comes from a working instrument

honest-null.definition: a working test that found no effect beyond a stated bound, a forecast that failed, or an error of our own found and fixed, reported with the same weight as a positive result
honest-null.excludes: a void run, and a result left unpublished because it was negative

verdict.definition: the pass or fail of one preregistered rule set against the run's numbers, read off by code
verdict.excludes: an interpretation written after reading the numbers

tier.definition: how ready a finding is to publish: A candidate, B signal worth expanding (B* strong), C internal, D honest null worth reporting, E not reliable as it stands
tier.excludes: a measure of how large or how true an effect is

rung.definition: where a claim stands logically: lead, hypothesis, thesis, conjecture, theorem, law candidate, or killed
rung.excludes: how ready the write-up is, which the tier records

standing.field: our findings ledger, after the citators used in law (KeyCite, Shepard's)
standing.definition: what later records did to a finding: held, extended, narrowed, questioned, refuted, retracted or superseded, computed from those records and never set by hand
standing.excludes: the finding's own verdict at the time it was run

findings-ledger.definition: the append-only, dated list of every result we have recorded, numbered F1, F2 and on; corrections are added as new dated lines and old entries are never rewritten

verified-line.definition: the closing statement of what was checked for publication, by what means, with what result and on what date; anything not checked is named as such
verified-line.excludes: a claim that the finding is true

p-value-draws.definition: the share of control draws scoring at or above the real score, with one added to the count and to the number of draws, so it is never zero
p-value-draws.excludes: a p value from a textbook formula that assumes a distribution

interval-95.definition: the range that holds the middle 95 percent of the bootstrap or control draws for a number; we report it beside the number
interval-95.excludes: a statement that the true value lies inside with 95 percent probability
